facts: Western grey kangaroos live in groups called mobs. More eyes and ears mean earlier warning of danger.
When a kangaroo senses danger it thumps the ground with its hind feet to warn the mob.
They graze mostly on grasses, feeding in the cooler hours around dawn and dusk.
Western grey kangaroos live across southern Australia, from Western Australia to western Victoria.
A joey stays in its mother's pouch for around nine months, then keeps feeding from her for months after.
Kangaroos can't walk backwards easily, which is one reason they're on Australia's coat of arms.
